learning_outcomes.text: Students know the most important standards used by today's internet.
Students know basic attack concepts on computer networks.
Students understand the connection between the individual layers of a computer network and the protocols contained therein.
Students can apply the most important network tools for analysis purposes.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to fundamental protocols and applications of computer networks
Standard protocols and algorithms in modern computer networks (e.g., the Internet)
Layer model based on a Top-Down approach
Routing algorithms in the Network Layer
teaching_methods: Moodle-supported homework with practical, computer-assisted exercises
Tool-of-the-Week: presentation, familiarization, and use of network-relevant computer analysis tools
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded upon successful completion of the exam. The exam score contributes to the final grade with a weight of 5/158 for B.Sc. Computer Science, 5/168 for B.Sc. Applied Computer Science, and 5/150 for B.Sc. IT Security / Information Technology.
bibliography: Computernetzwerke: Der Top-Down Ansatz by Kurose and Ross (Pearson Verlag)
